title: 6 Best Zonka Feedback Alternatives for Customer Feedback Analytics
summary: The best Zonka Feedback alternatives: Thematic, Qualtrics, Medallia, SurveySparrow, Chattermill, Kapiche. Which half of Zonka you replace decides the answer.
body_markdown:
Search for Zonka Feedback alternatives and almost every page lists survey tools: SurveySparrow, SurveyMonkey, Typeform, Jotform, Qualaroo. That answers half the question. Zonka sells two things: a customer feedback platform that collects, and an AI Feedback Intelligence platform that analyzes. Which alternative you want depends on which half stopped working.


If the analysis is what stopped working, the best Zonka Feedback alternative for customer feedback analytics is Thematic. Thematic builds a[two-level theme taxonomy](https://getthematic.com/insights/ai-powered-customer-feedback-theme-discovery) from your feedback itself rather than from a template. It links each theme to its[measured impact](https://getthematic.com/insights/link-feedback-themes-nps-csat-drivers) on net promoter score (NPS) or customer satisfaction score (CSAT), and reports[which themes moved the score](https://getthematic.com/insights/quantify-themes-moved-nps-score) between two periods. Every theme traces back to the raw comments underneath it, so a skeptical executive can interrogate the number rather than take it on faith.


If collection is the problem, you want a survey platform, not an analytics layer. SurveySparrow is the closest like-for-like there. Qualtrics and Medallia replace both halves at once for enterprises that would rather consolidate. Chattermill and Kapiche are the other dedicated analysis layers worth a look.


Below is the shortlist, a test for which half you're replacing, where each option wins, and what to ask before signing.


## The list at a glance


1. **Thematic** : enterprise customer experience (CX) and insights teams replacing the analysis half, keeping their existing collection.
2. **Qualtrics with XM Discover** : enterprises replacing both halves who want survey distribution and conversational analytics from one vendor.
3. **Medallia** : organizations replacing both halves who want text analytics inside a broad experience management suite.
4. **SurveySparrow** : teams replacing the collection half, mid-market, who want a familiar survey builder and per-response pricing.
5. **Chattermill** : large CX-led brands replacing the analysis half across many languages and business units.
6. **Kapiche** : mid-market insights teams replacing the analysis half who want a fast first result on survey feedback. Here is the same shortlist side by side, with Zonka as the baseline.

## Which half of Zonka are you replacing?


Zonka is a bundled suite, and the gap between[feedback management and feedback analytics](https://getthematic.com/insights/customer-feedback-analytics-vs-management-difference) is the whole of this decision. So be accurate about what Zonka does before shopping. On the collection side it runs surveys over email, SMS, WhatsApp, website, in-product, an in-app software development kit (SDK), kiosks, QR codes, and offline. On the analysis side, its AI Feedback Intelligence platform takes in surveys, tickets, reviews, chats, and calls. It does theme and sub-theme discovery, sentiment analysis, entity and aspect tracking, and impact scoring. It connects to Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk, Jira, and Slack.


So the useful question isn't "what's better than Zonka." It's which of these three describes you.


- **The surveys are fine, the analysis isn't.** Your open-text volume grew, or feedback now arrives from channels the survey tool never owned.[Integrating those sources](https://getthematic.com/insights/integrate-feedback-sources-analytics-platform) into one view is the job. Go to items 1, 5, and 6.
- **The analysis is fine, the collection isn't.** You need a different builder, different distribution, or different per-response economics. Go to item 4.
- **You want one vendor for both, at enterprise scale.** Go to items 2 and 3. One note on cost. Zonka prices the two halves on[separate meters](https://www.zonkafeedback.com/pricing) : Feedback Management on number of responses, AI Feedback Intelligence on data credits. Neither is published, so every comparison needs a quote. Worth knowing before you assume a replacement costs more.


## 1. Thematic


**Thematic** is the customer intelligence layer for enterprise CX, insights, and product teams that have to defend their themes to someone who will push back. It analyzes unstructured feedback from surveys, support tickets, call transcripts, app reviews, and social, and sits on top of the existing stack rather than replacing it.


The difference from Zonka's analysis half is what happens to a theme after it's found. Thematic builds the taxonomy bottom-up, so the structure emerges from the feedback rather than from categories written two years ago. There's no rebuild cycle when customers change how they talk. Analysts can inspect, merge, split, and edit that structure directly. Thematic quantifies each theme's impact on NPS or CSAT, and separately reports score change across two periods. So a team reports "billing confusion cost 5 points, faster resolution gained 4" instead of "NPS dropped 3 points." Every theme clicks through to the raw comments underneath it.


The architecture is the point for anyone leaving only half of Zonka. Smith and Smith, the vehicle glass repair company, collects feedback in Qualtrics across every location and journey point. It discovers themes and ties them to NPS impact in Thematic, then distributes through Power BI. Their Senior Insights Analyst, Carlos Reyes, was direct that the survey platform's own text analysis wasn't advanced enough to answer the questions his team kept getting.


On outcomes: One New Zealand, the connectivity provider then trading as Vodafone New Zealand, used Thematic on its touchpoint NPS (tNPS) verbatim comments and sentiment. That replaced the manual reading of hundreds of thousands of comments a year. It saved 60 hours every month and recorded a double-digit tNPS increase within nine months, with NPS Evolution Manager Tania Parangi reporting a positive return on investment. Forrester Consulting, in a[Total Economic Impact study](https://getthematic.com/forrester-total-economic-impact-study) commissioned by Thematic, measured a 543% three-year return on investment with payback in under six months.


**The trade-off.** Thematic doesn't collect feedback. It's the analysis half, not a like-for-like Zonka replacement. If you need one vendor to send the survey and analyze the responses, Thematic is half the answer and a survey platform is the other half.


## 2. Qualtrics with XM Discover


**Qualtrics** is the consolidation answer for enterprises that want survey distribution and conversational analytics from one vendor. Its text analytics arm, XM Discover, was formerly Clarabridge. It analyzes cases, chat, voice transcriptions, email, surveys, and third-party reviews, extracting intent, emotion, effort, and sentiment.


Where it wins is contact-center-grade analysis at scale. If you outgrew Zonka on call and chat volume rather than survey volume, this is the most direct step up.


**The trade-off.** Cost and complexity, and the gap is large. XM Discover is reported to run as a $300,000 to $400,000 per year add-on, on top of a base platform starting around $25,000 per year. Taxonomy setup in Designer needs specialists and ongoing maintenance. A team moving from a bundled mid-market suite should scope both carefully.


## 3. Medallia


**Medallia** suits organizations that want text analytics inside a broad experience management suite rather than as a separate layer. Its in-platform text analytics parses verbatims at the phrase level, sorts them into topic hierarchies, and applies sentiment. It also offers impact scoring that shows how topics move NPS, the capability most directly comparable to Zonka's own.


The breadth is real. Collection, analysis, and program management sit in one place, which is the argument for consolidating onto one enterprise vendor rather than assembling two.


**The trade-off.** Weight. Setup and ongoing taxonomy management take real internal time. A team that chose Zonka partly because it was quick to stand up should scope that before committing.


## 4. SurveySparrow


**SurveySparrow** is the closest like-for-like on the collection half, and one of the tools most consistently named in third-party Zonka round-ups. It's the right pick if your survey builder, distribution, or per-response economics are the actual problem.


Pricing is[published and metered by responses](https://surveysparrow.com/pricing/) : 2,500 on Basic, 15,000 on Starter, 36,000 on Business, custom at Enterprise. That transparency is useful when Zonka quotes rather than lists.


**The trade-off.** Two things are gated. Additional users are billed at $49 per user per month, so a program that wants wide read-only access gets expensive fast. And Key Driver Analysis, its driver-analysis feature, is Enterprise-tier only, as is auto-translate across 130+ languages. If analysis depth is why you're leaving Zonka, a survey platform is unlikely to be the fix.


## 5. Chattermill


**Chattermill** fits large, CX-led enterprises replacing the analysis half across high volumes and many languages. It unifies surveys, reviews, social, support conversations, and voice, then applies deep-learning aspect-based sentiment analysis to surface the drivers behind an experience.


Chattermill analyzes feedback in more than 100 languages, with automated translation and transcription built in. It connects with more than 65 feedback channels, and carries[SOC 2](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/resources/landing/system-and-organization-controls-soc-suite-of-services) Type II and ISO 27001:2022. If your Zonka program hit a language or channel wall, this is the most direct step up.


**The trade-off.** Chattermill is analytics-oriented by design. It's strong at telling a team what's trending and weaker at driving the next action, so it surfaces the theme without filing the ticket. Pricing is custom and quoted, so you're back in the same quote-to-quote comparison you were in with Zonka.


## 6. Kapiche


**Kapiche** fits mid-market and enterprise insights teams that want fast topic discovery on survey and conversation feedback. It applies natural language processing with no manual code-frame setup, then layers on sentiment, topic clustering, taxonomy classification, and churn and escalation forecasting. The appeal is speed to a first useful result, close to what a Zonka user is used to.


**The trade-off.** Scale, and it arrives as a hard number. Kapiche prices per project, with row limits running from 50,000 to 250,000 by tier. Its Bronze tier starts at $1,060 per month, and its integration ecosystem is narrower than the enterprise incumbents. If you're leaving because you hit a ceiling, check where the next one sits before you sign.


## How to choose between them


The right pick depends on which half broke. Ask these during a demo, and insist on seeing each one run against your own feedback.


- **Which half are we actually replacing?** Answer this before you shortlist. A survey platform won't fix an analysis problem, and an analysis layer won't send your surveys.
- **Can it take every source we have, not just surveys?** List your channels first, then ask. Tickets and reviews are easy. Call transcripts, in-product feedback, and chat logs are where gaps show up.
- **Can we see and edit the theme taxonomy?** A good answer shows you the themes, lets you merge or split them, and traces each back to the underlying comments. A vague answer means a black box.
- **Can it tell us which themes moved the score, not just which are most common?** Ask for a score change breakdown across two periods. Frequency without impact sends teams to fix the loudest complaint rather than the costliest one.
- **What's metered, and what does it cost at our volume?** Zonka meters responses and data credits separately. Others meter rows, records, or seats. Get every meter named and priced against your real numbers, setup and services included.
- **How long until the first reliable report?** Hours or days is strong. Weeks of model training or code-frame setup is a heavier lift than a mid-market replacement warrants.


## The short version


If you're leaving Zonka Feedback because the analysis stopped keeping up with your open-text volume or channel mix, Thematic is the strongest alternative: themes built bottom-up from your own data, quantified impact on the score, and every theme traceable to the comments behind it. Keep collecting wherever you collect today and add the layer on top, the way Smith and Smith does.


If collection is the problem, SurveySparrow is the closest like-for-like and publishes its response tiers. If you'd rather consolidate onto one enterprise vendor, Qualtrics with XM Discover and Medallia are the two to compare, and both are a significant step up in cost and setup.


The fastest way to decide is to run the same batch of your own feedback through your top two, then ask each vendor to show you exactly how one theme was built and how much of the last score change it explains. If you can defend the number to your CFO, you've found your tool.


If your shortlist reaches past this page, Thematic compares the field against other incumbents in its guides to[Qualtrics alternatives](https://getthematic.com/insights/qualtrics-competitors-and-alternatives) ,[Medallia alternatives](https://getthematic.com/insights/top-medallia-alternatives) , and[Chattermill alternatives](https://getthematic.com/insights/chattermill-alternatives-and-competitors) .
